description: Binding-K SDP solver — operator-selection LP / shadow-price / primal-dual / lp-duality search for the binding operator K(𝔥) ∈ H_{3·A}(q_0) factor of the canonical T_w(𝔥) under the decomposition T_w(𝔥) = K(𝔥) · ⊗_i T_w(nucleon_i) per the deliverable-4 binding-K finding (PR #610). Issue #604 items 1-5: extends the H_3-only rho-prefactor verifier to the atomic strand count n_0 = 3·A using the existing build_seminormal_matrices (general-n Hoefsmit was already in hecke_characters.py — no new combinatorial code needed). Computes K's per-Wedderburn-block PSD eigenvalues, dominant λ* ⊢ 3·A by |y_λ · χ_λ(K)|, and tests the four candidate ρ rules against observed ρ for ²H (n_0=6), ³H (n_0=9, embedded 8_11), ³He (n_0=9, embedded L6a4). The natural Wedderburn-PSD constraint at the atomic strand count becomes ρ_λ(K) ⪰ 0 — the 'binding stability' certificate; per-atom witnesses include LP primal/dual (y0_star, y_star, active_set, primal_obj, dual_obj, duality_gap) per CLAUDE.md 'LP/SDP duals — first-class infra'.

lp_dual.interpretation: argmin t = dominant Wedderburn block λ*(K) of the binding operator K ∈ H_{n_0}(q_0); the LP dual y_star marks the saturating block.  Per conj:rho-prefactor-structural, ρ(𝔥) = round(dim_q(λ*(K))).

explicit_binding_k_heuristic.binding_interpretation: σ_3^2 — Hopf link crossing strand 3 of proton with strand 4 of neutron in B_6.  Standard Hopf representation.

explicit_binding_k_heuristic.binding_interpretation: σ_3 σ_4 σ_6 σ_7 — heuristic; the true 8_11-class binding link in B_9 involves more crossings.  Diagnostic only.

explicit_binding_k_heuristic.binding_interpretation: σ_3 σ_6 — heuristic: two Hopf-like crossings binding strand 3 of nucleon 1 to strand 4 of nucleon 2, AND strand 6 of nucleon 2 to strand 7 of nucleon 3 in B_9. The true L6a4 link has 3 components and a richer braid representation; this is a single-crossing surrogate for diagnostic comparison only.

summary.framework_status: operational — general-n Hoefsmit + binding-K factorisation + per-block ρ-rule evaluation + LP/SDP dual emission wired end-to-end at H_{3·A} for ²H, ³H, ³He.
summary.verdict: 0 of 4 candidate rules reproduce ρ at H_{3·A} for all 3 atoms.  Compare with the H_3-level evaluation (rho-prefactor-structural-verifier.witness.json, deliverable 4 of PR #610) which had 0/5 rules consistent due to the proton vs ³He χ-collision: that collision is resolved here by the H_{3·A} embedding via the binding operator K.
what_remains_open: Categorical uniqueness theorem for binding-K (deliverable 3): per atom, prove K(𝔥) is the unique PSD-feasible Hecke element satisfying the joint-tower SDP cross-level consistency constraints (4) of prop:joint-tower-sdp-confinement.  The constituent leg is closed by R5-minimal; the binding-K leg is the open core.
Generalise to ⁴He (B_? at H_12), ⁶Li (H_18), ⁷Li (H_21), α-cluster atoms — the same factorisation should apply.
Symbolic-q evaluation of K's Wedderburn structure to discharge the rounding question categorically.

caveats: Numerical evaluation at f64 precision; deuteron uses H_6 (11 partitions, max d_λ = 16), tritium and ³He use H_9 (30 partitions, max d_λ = 42).  The Wenzl-Schur weights y_λ(q_0) for n=6, 9 are loaded from y-lambda-wenzl-witness.json if present; otherwise a uniform 1/|P(n)| fallback is used (the dominant-λ identification is dominated by χ_λ for typical knot elements).  K is computed via the braid-word concatenation T_atom · cp^{-1}, NOT via per-block matrix inversion (avoids ill-conditioned blocks).
